<observation>
  <type>feature</type>
  <title>Added EVAL_REPEAT_ALL mode to GoldenSetEvaluator for run-to-run variance measurement</title>
  <subtitle>Golden-set evaluation can now repeat every sample EVAL_KEY_REPEAT times and records promptTokens per scored sample.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>GoldenSetEvaluator.java replaces the keySample-only repeat branch (`int runs = sample.keySample ? keyRepeat : 1;`) with a `boolean repeatAll = "1".equals(envOr("EVAL_REPEAT_ALL", "0"));` flag that repeats every sample when enabled.</fact>
    <fact>GoldenSetScorer.java adds a new `public final int promptTokens` field, growing the constructor from the previous call ending in `null, 0, false`.</fact>
    <fact>scripts/eval-model-quality.sh documents `EVAL_REPEAT_ALL=1` as repeating every sample `EVAL_KEY_REPEAT` times to measure run-to-run variance.</fact>
    <fact>The change spans 3 files with 222 insertions and 14 deletions, all in test/eval code and its shell wrapper.</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The golden-set model-quality harness gained two capabilities. First, `GoldenSetEvaluator` previously repeated only designated key samples (`sample.keySample ? keyRepeat : 1`); a new `EVAL_REPEAT_ALL` environment variable (default "0") lets the operator repeat every sample `EVAL_KEY_REPEAT` times so run-to-run variance can be measured across the whole golden set rather than only a subset. Second, `GoldenSetScorer` now exposes a `public final int promptTokens` field so prompt token usage is captured per scored sample. The wrapper script `scripts/eval-model-quality.sh` documents the new flag. This matters because without repeat-all mode, evaluation could not quantify run-to-run variance, and prompt token cost was not tracked.</narrative>
